task: Local worker VM disks (sparse linked clones) keep growing after #574/#575. Measure the writers, change only what the evidence justifies, and add guards that catch growth early.

events.summary: Add guards only: one PrometheusRule alert, a host-side advisory check, a runbook section and an R-check. Deliberately left alone: Trivy, kopia/Velero, retention, log rotation (no writer large enough to justify a change), any VM destroy/recreate (another lane owns it), Kakao cluster.

Prometheus over 72h: worker steady median 8-27 GB/day but single hours of 44-144 GB; control planes 27-54 GB/day (etcd, NFS) with vmdks of 9-25G; worker-2 host vmdk 82G vs guest 44G used. Journals 118-310M, pod logs 25-72M, kopia-maintain hourly.

NodeDiskWriteRateHigh (6h average above 20 GB/day for 30m, workers only), check-vm-disk.sh (vmdk dir vs guest df, host free space, run warn-only by up.sh) and the operations.md section 12 reclaim runbook.

events.scope: Static regression suite, promtool behavior cases for the alert, the check script against live VMs (flags worker-2 at 82G vs 44G, others OK) and the rule loaded in the live Prometheus after push-to-gitea. NOT covered: a real alert firing on a sustained worker burst, Kakao, any VM reclaim.
evidence: test:python3 scripts/test/lib/check-vm-disk-guards.py --mutation-verify -> 10 mutations caught, 4 promtool cases passed
test:live local cluster: Prometheus /api/v1/rules lists NodeDiskWriteRateHigh after push-to-gitea

events.summary: In the repository and on the local cluster the growth guards exist and are pinned by R309. Disk growth itself is not stopped: steady worker writes remain and the vmdk can only be reclaimed by recreating the node.

Complete for the guard scope within repository and local-cluster scope; growth itself is not eliminated, no other writer was changed, and Trivy scan Job layer writes and install-cni attribution remain unmeasured.
